note: heuristic-v0's memory, latency-pressure and batch-demand rules, behind an overload regime. Shares and loads are against the reference profile over the classes that wanted CPU. Overload starts when the CPU is contended (busy >= contended_bp), batch wants CPU, and either latency is saturated at its reference share (load >= saturated_bp) with a backlog whose oldest job waited stall_wait_us, or latency runs above its reference share while batch holds less than batch_floor_bp of its own. Overload holds the reference profile until latency load falls under release_bp. saturated_bp and contended_bp sit 5% under a full share; batch_floor_bp is objective-v2's batch_retain_bp; release_bp leaves a 10-point band so a share pinned at the even split cannot flip the regime. stall_wait_us is the only fitted value: see derivation and aik_controller.tune. Development, calibration and the sealed splits were not read to set it. Calibration and sealed feature ranges were inspected while the rule was designed, so they are development evidence for v1, not held-out evidence.
